question: What do you call a Glycocalyx that is a loose sheath type?
solution:
The Correct answer is **Slime Layer**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glycocalyx**__:

 __
 
• It is a **surface layer that covers the cell membrane of many bacteria**, epithelial cells or other cells.
 
• It is made up of proteoglycans, glycoproteins and glycolipids.
 
• Glycocalyx is a viscous polysaccharide or **polypeptide slime that covers microbes.**
 
• It enhances adherence to surfaces. resists phagocytic engulfment by the white blood cells.
 
• It **prevents antibiotics from contacting the microbe.**
 
 
 
• **Functions**__:
 
 
• ​It protects the cell from **dehydration** (capsule).
 
• It protects the bacterial cell from engulfment and destruction by the immune system's white blood cells (capsule).
 
• Glycocalyx gives the bacterial cell a **sticky character which enables it to attach to surfaces**.
 
• Glycocalyx also helps the bacterial cells to adhere to each other.
 
• This forms a bacterial aggregate that can't be engulfed by the immune cells.
